editorial:
Imagine you are an actor who just cannot get a break because of how you look. That is exactly where you find Edward. He is tired of being judged, so he decides to get a wild medical surgery to completely change his face. At first, it seems like a dream come true. He gets the looks he always wanted and suddenly the world treats him better. The vibe is a weird mix of funny and sad, making you wonder if changing your outside actually fixes the problems on the inside.

Sebastian Eugene Hanover does an amazing job showing how Edward loses himself. The way the story shifts from a hopeful start to a stressful mess is really gripping. While some parts move a bit slow, the payoff is totally worth it. You should definitely watch this if you like stories that mess with your head. For the best experience, try renting it on Apple TV or streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see all the detail in the makeup. If you are a movie collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your shelf is a great move.
endingExplained: By the end, Edward realizes that his new face did not solve his life problems; it just created new ones. He becomes obsessed with his identity and the people who now love the fake version of him. The movie wraps up with him facing the reality that he can never truly go back to who he was. It ends on a dark note, showing that trying to erase your past usually leads to a total breakdown.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological stories with a twist.
